title: ThetaEvolve: Test-time Learning on Open Problems

parentSelection: Database-based single-parent sampling; exact archive/population sampling rule unclear

mechanism.domainTask: Program evolution for open mathematical optimization and test-time RL
mechanism.populationDetail: The inherited OpenEvolve database assigns candidates to persistent island subpopulations and organizes candidates within each island by MAP-Elites feature cells.
mechanism.archiveDetail: A separate global archive tracks multiple top-performing programs across all islands for exploitation-based sampling; MAP-Elites cell incumbents are the diversity-preserving population structure.
mechanism.replacementDetail: A child inherits its parent's island absent an island switch, competes with the incumbent in its feature cell, and may later be removed by global capacity cleanup; the global elite archive is maintained separately.
mechanism.generationDetail: The model emits SEARCH/REPLACE diff blocks that the parser applies to one selected parent program to form a child.
mechanism.feedbackDetail: Parent programs are accompanied by evaluation results in prompts, and scores/validity outcomes are used by database ranking and sampling. Task-specific reward shaping transforms scalar scores during RL training.
mechanism.parentSelectionDetail: Each of B independently sampled parent programs seeds its own prompt; B is batch size, while each child has one parent. The paper does not specify whether a selected parent was drawn from the global elite archive or another island/database structure, nor the exact selection distribution.
mechanism.outOfTaxonomy: The dynamic evolutionary environment is coupled with online GRPO training of the LLM at test time, so model parameters learn from programs generated in the evolving database; this model-training/search coupling is not represented by the current taxonomy fields.

provenance.sourcePdf: papers/ThetaEvolve Test-time Learning on Open Problems.pdf
provenance.citationWarning: The survey currently places ThetaEvolve under flat populations and large-scale modification. The paper describes persistent islands with within-island MAP-Elites cells and a global elite archive; it applies SEARCH/REPLACE diffs to one parent. Database sampling is described through inherited OpenEvolve behavior, but exact parent-selection probabilities and any adaptive explore-exploit controller are not provided. Supplied paper copy is labeled preprint.
